Tropical rain forests have high rainfall and warm temperatures, which accelerate decomposition and nutrient cycling, but heavy rainfall also causes significant leaching of nutrients from the soil.  
Tundra has slow decomposition due to cold temperatures, so nutrients remain locked in organic matter.  
Taiga (boreal forest) also has cold temperatures and slow nutrient cycling.  
Deserts have low rainfall and minimal leaching, with slow nutrient cycling due to low biological activity.  
Thus, tropical rain forests have the highest rate of leaching and nutrient cycling.  

Final answer: (A)
